title: The Real Cost of a 3D-Printed Hypercar

scenes.text: What does a three-D-printed hypercar really cost? The reported price of a Czinger 21C is one point seven million dollars. But that is the price tag, not the cost. The cost includes thousands of hours of labour, a company that has raised hundreds of millions of dollars, and years of delay. We pulled every number our sources give, and we show where they stop.
scenes.caption: THE REAL COST OF A 3D-PRINTED HYPERCAR

scenes.text: Our sources are Backfire News, via Yahoo, from March twenty twenty-four; GTPlanet, from February twenty twenty; Wikipedia's pages on the Czinger 21C and the McLaren Senna; CSQ; ASME; Autocar and GoAuto. Where numbers conflict, we show both. Our own arithmetic is labelled, and anything the sources do not say is flagged as not stated.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: BACKFIRE NEWS (19 MAR 2024) · GTPLANET (21 FEB 2020) · WIKIPEDIA (21C, SENNA) · CSQ (SEP 2022) · ASME (27 MAR 2025) · AUTOCAR · GOAUTO (11 DEC 2017) · CONFLICTS SHOWN · OUR ARITHMETIC LABELLED

scenes.text: Start with the sticker. The Backfire News report, published on the nineteenth of March twenty twenty-four, gives a price of one point seven million dollars for the Czinger 21C, a tandem two-seater limited to eighty cars. That is the only explicit price in the sources we read from the last two years. We could not find a Czinger price list.
scenes.caption: BACKFIRE NEWS VIA YAHOO (19 MAR 2024): $1.7 MILLION; LIMITED TO 80; TANDEM TWO-SEATER · OFFICIAL PRICE LIST: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Four years earlier, the number was different. GTPlanet, in February twenty twenty, said the price was unconfirmed, and told readers not to expect a change from two million dollars. By our arithmetic, that is three hundred thousand dollars above the later report, a difference of about eighteen percent of one point seven million.
scenes.caption: GTPLANET (21 FEB 2020): PRICE UNCONFIRMED, 'DON'T EXPECT A CHANGE FROM $2M' · $2.0 M − $1.7 M = $0.3 M = 17.6% OF 1.7 M (OUR ARITHMETIC) · WHY THE FIGURE MOVED: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Why the number moved is not stated anywhere. It might be that the early figure was a rounded guess, that the company changed the price, or that two writers used different assumptions. We can only say the price has been reported at two million and at one point seven million, in different years, and that neither source cites a price list.
scenes.caption: PRICE REPORTED AT $2 M (2020) AND $1.7 M (2024) · CAUSE OF DIFFERENCE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · NEITHER SOURCE CITES A PRICE LIST

scenes.text: If every one of the eighty cars sold at the lower figure, then by our arithmetic the run is worth about one hundred thirty-six million dollars. At two million, it is one hundred sixty million. That is a simple multiplication, not a revenue figure: the sources do not say how many cars are sold, whether prices differ by version, or what options cost.
scenes.caption: 80 × $1.7 M = $136 M · 80 × $2.0 M = $160 M (OUR ARITHMETIC; NOT A REVENUE FIGURE) · CARS SOLD, VERSION PRICES, OPTION COSTS: NOT STATED · BLACKBIRD (4 CARS) PRICE: NOT STATED

scenes.text: The price per horsepower is another way to see it, with caveats. At one point seven million dollars and Wikipedia's twelve hundred fifty horsepower, our arithmetic gives about thirteen hundred sixty dollars for each horsepower. At two million, sixteen hundred. Using Backfire's own thirteen thirty-one horsepower, it is about twelve hundred eighty. The answer depends on which source you trust.
scenes.caption: $1.7 M ÷ 1,250 HP = $1,360/HP · $2.0 M ÷ 1,250 = $1,600/HP · $1.7 M ÷ 1,331 HP (BACKFIRE) = $1,277/HP (OUR ARITHMETIC; HORSEPOWER FIGURES CONFLICT ACROSS SOURCES)

scenes.text: Here is the number that gets closest to real cost. Backfire News says each Czinger 21C takes three thousand to four thousand hours of labour. The article does not say what the hours include, such as machine time, assembly, engineering or testing, and it does not give a cost per hour. But it is the clearest measure of effort we have.
scenes.caption: BACKFIRE (19 MAR 2024): 3,000–4,000 LABOR HOURS PER CAR · WHAT IS INCLUDED (MACHINE TIME, ASSEMBLY, ENGINEERING): NOT STATED · COST PER HOUR: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Put it in human terms. A full-time worker, by our arithmetic, works about two thousand eighty hours in a year, using forty hours a week for fifty-two weeks. So one car is roughly one and a half to two person-years of work. That sounds enormous for a car sold to one customer, but remember the cars are built by teams, not individuals.
scenes.caption: 40 H × 52 WEEKS = 2,080 H/YEAR · 3,000 ÷ 2,080 = 1.44 · 4,000 ÷ 2,080 = 1.92 PERSON-YEARS PER CAR (OUR ARITHMETIC; REAL SHIFT PATTERNS NOT STATED)

scenes.text: Now the whole run. Eighty cars at three thousand to four thousand hours is two hundred forty thousand to three hundred twenty thousand hours, by our arithmetic. Divided by two thousand eighty hours a year, that is a hundred fifteen to a hundred fifty-four full-time person-years of work for the planned total, before the Blackbirds.
scenes.caption: 80 × 3,000 = 240,000 H · 80 × 4,000 = 320,000 H · ÷ 2,080 = 115–154 PERSON-YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC; BLACKBIRD HOURS NOT STATED)

scenes.text: Can a small company do that? CSQ reported in September twenty twenty-two that Czinger Vehicles had fewer than fifty employees. By our arithmetic, fifty people give about a hundred four thousand hours a year. So two hundred forty to three hundred twenty thousand hours would take them roughly two and a third to three years, if they did all the work themselves.
scenes.caption: CSQ (SEP 2022): CZINGER VEHICLES < 50 EMPLOYEES · 50 × 2,080 = 104,000 H/YEAR · 240,000 ÷ 104,000 = 2.3 · 320,000 ÷ 104,000 = 3.1 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC; ASSUMES ALL HOURS BY THOSE 50; THEY DO NOT SAY THAT)

scenes.text: That calculation is only an illustration. The sources do not say who does the hours, how many people work on the cars today, or whether sister company Divergent supplies parts and labour. But it shows why timing matters. At that effort, by our arithmetic, a company of that size would need several years for eighty cars, and the sources say deliveries were planned across several years.
scenes.caption: ILLUSTRATION ONLY · CURRENT HEADCOUNT, DIVISION OF WORK WITH DIVERGENT: NOT STATED · WIKIPEDIA: DELIVERIES PLANNED Q4 2023, MOST 2024

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, here is another illustration. If the whole one point seven million dollars were spent on those hours, it would be about four hundred twenty-five to five hundred sixty-seven dollars an hour. In reality, the price also covers parts, printing, development, profit and everything else. We offer the figure as a ceiling, not an hourly rate.
scenes.caption: $1.7 M ÷ 4,000 H = $425/H · $1.7 M ÷ 3,000 H = $567/H (OUR ARITHMETIC; PRICE ALSO COVERS PARTS, DEVELOPMENT, PROFIT: NOT A LABOR RATE)

scenes.text: The pitch for printed construction is that it avoids tooling. ASME says printed parts let engineers make, test and improve a part without waiting for tooling, and that the process frees designs from limits such as draft angle and tool access. That is a saving in time and flexibility. The article does not give a dollar figure for what it saves.
scenes.caption: ASME (27 MAR 2025): NO WAITING FOR TOOLING; FREEDOM FROM DRAFT-ANGLE, WALL-THICKNESS, TOOL-ACCESS LIMITS · DOLLAR SAVING: NOT STATED · 'SPECIFIC COST-REDUCTION FIGURES': NOT STATED
scenes.chapter: What toolless building does and does not save

scenes.text: Tooling matters most when you build many identical cars. A stamped steel panel has a huge up-front cost, then each part is cheap. For an eighty-car run, the up-front cost is spread over very few cars. That logic is our reading, not a quote from a source, but it explains why a printed approach could make sense for a hypercar.
scenes.caption: OUR READING (NOT A SOURCE STATEMENT): TOOLING COST ÷ FEW CARS = HIGH PER-CAR COST; PRINTING AVOIDS IT · NO SOURCE GIVES TOOLING COSTS FOR ANY CAR

scenes.text: But printing has its own cost. Facfox reports that Divergent bought five pre-production metal printers from SLM Solutions in twenty nineteen and planned twenty next-generation systems. The sources give no price for these machines. ASME also says early parts suffered from porosity and print-orientation problems. Fixing that took development effort that is part of the real cost.
scenes.caption: FACFOX: 5 PRE-PRODUCTION SLM SYSTEMS (2019), PLAN FOR 20 NEXT-GEN SYSTEMS · PRINTER PRICES: NOT STATED · ASME: EARLY POROSITY + PRINT-ORIENTATION ISSUES, LATER RESOLVED · DEVELOPMENT COST: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Then there is the money raised. CSQ's September twenty twenty-two article quotes Kevin Czinger saying Divergent recently brought in two hundred fifty million dollars, and that Czinger Vehicles and Divergent together have raised close to five hundred million. It names investors including John Thornton and Tom Steyer.
scenes.caption: CSQ (SEP 2022), KEVIN CZINGER: DIVERGENT 'RECENTLY BROUGHT IN' $250 MILLION; CZINGER VEHICLES + DIVERGENT 'CLOSE TO $500 MILLION' RAISED · INVESTORS NAMED: JOHN THORNTON, TOM STEYER

scenes.text: A careful point. By our arithmetic, five hundred million dollars divided by eighty cars is six point two five million dollars a car, which is nearly four times the one point seven million price. But that comparison is unfair, because the money funds Divergent's wider business, not only the 21C. The sources do not say how the funds were split.
scenes.caption: $500 M ÷ 80 = $6.25 M PER CAR · $6.25 M ÷ $1.7 M = 3.7× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · UNFAIR AS A CAR COST: MONEY ALSO FUNDS DIVERGENT'S OTHER BUSINESS · SPLIT: NOT STATED

scenes.text: What the comparison does show is scale. A car priced at one point seven million dollars is only the visible part of a project funded at a far larger level. CSQ also says Divergent had about five hundred twenty patents, according to Kevin Czinger. The article does not value the patents, and we do not guess a value.
scenes.caption: CSQ: ABOUT 520 PATENTS (PER KEVIN CZINGER) · PATENT VALUE: NOT STATED · 'SCALE' READING = OUR FRAMING

scenes.text: To judge a hypercar price, it helps to compare. McLaren's Senna was announced in December twenty seventeen at seven hundred fifty thousand pounds, according to Autocar and GoAuto. GoAuto converted that to about one point three million Australian dollars. Wikipedia says the Senna was limited to five hundred cars.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR + GOAUTO (11 DEC 2017): £750,000 (A$1.3 M); WIKIPEDIA: 500 UNITS · LIST PRICE ONLY; OPTIONS EXTRA
scenes.chapter: The McLaren Senna as a yardstick

scenes.text: Autocar adds that buyers can add extras through McLaren Special Operations, and that virtually all customers will. So the real invoice for a Senna was likely higher than the list price, though our sources give no average. By our arithmetic, five hundred cars at the list price come to three hundred seventy-five million pounds, before any options.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR: MSO EXTRAS — 'VIRTUALLY ALL CUSTOMERS WILL' ADD · 500 × £750,000 = £375 M (OUR ARITHMETIC; LIST PRICE, EXCLUDES OPTIONS) · AVERAGE OPTION SPEND: NOT STATED

scenes.text: What happened afterwards tells us about value. Wikipedia says the last Senna sold at auction for one million nine hundred sixteen thousand seven hundred ninety-three pounds. By our arithmetic, that is two and a half times the list price, a gain of one million one hundred sixty-six thousand seven hundred ninety-three pounds. The page does not say when or where the sale took place.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA (SENNA): FINAL CAR SOLD AT AUCTION £1,916,793 · £1,916,793 − £750,000 = £1,166,793; ÷ 750,000 = 2.56× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · DATE + AUCTION HOUSE: NOT STATED · ONE CAR, NOT A MARKET AVERAGE

scenes.text: That is one car. It may have been special as the final one built, and the sources do not say what a typical Senna sells for. So we cannot say the model gained two and a half times for everyone. For the Czinger, we found no auction or resale result in our sources at all. A buyer today has no sourced market to check.
scenes.caption: ONE CAR ≠ MARKET (OUR READING) · TYPICAL SENNA RESALE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · CZINGER 21C RESALE / AUCTION RESULTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The two price tags also come from different currencies and years, so we do not compare them directly. The Senna at seven hundred fifty thousand pounds in twenty seventeen and the Czinger at one point seven million dollars in twenty twenty-four are not on a common footing. Our sources give no exchange rates or inflation figures, and we will not invent them.
scenes.caption: £750,000 (2017) vs $1.7 M (2024): DIFFERENT CURRENCY + YEAR · EXCHANGE RATES / INFLATION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · NO DIRECT COMPARISON MADE

scenes.text: Price per horsepower is at least in each car's own currency. The Senna is seven hundred fifty thousand pounds for seven hundred eighty-nine horsepower, by our arithmetic about nine hundred fifty pounds a horsepower. The Czinger is about thirteen hundred sixty dollars. Different money, so not comparable, but both are in the high hundreds or low thousands per horsepower.
scenes.caption: £750,000 ÷ 789 HP = £951/HP · $1.7 M ÷ 1,250 HP = $1,360/HP (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT CURRENCIES, DIFFERENT YEARS)

scenes.text: Waiting is part of the price. The Senna's timeline was short. It was revealed online in December twenty seventeen and, Wikipedia says, deliveries began in the third quarter of twenty eighteen. By our arithmetic, that is seven to nine months from reveal to the first customer deliveries.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: SENNA ONLINE REVEAL 10 DEC 2017; DELIVERIES Q3 2018 (JUL–SEP) · 7–9 MONTHS (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Czinger's timeline was longer. It was unveiled on the eleventh of March twenty twenty. Wikipedia says deliveries were planned for the fourth quarter of twenty twenty-three, with most in twenty twenty-four. By our arithmetic, that is about three years and seven months or more from unveiling to the first planned deliveries, roughly five to six times the Senna's wait.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 21C UNVEILED 11 MAR 2020; DELIVERIES PLANNED Q4 2023, MOST 2024 · ~43–45 MONTHS vs 7–9 MONTHS = 4.8–6.4× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ACTUAL DELIVERY DATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Backfire News says production was anticipated to begin in twenty twenty-two and that a chip shortage delayed it. Wikipedia describes the Geneva show cancellation in twenty twenty. Neither source says what customers paid in deposits or whether anyone waited with money tied up. Deposits are a real cost for a buyer, but they are not in our sources.
scenes.caption: BACKFIRE: PRODUCTION 'ANTICIPATED' 2022, CHIP SHORTAGE DELAYED · WIKIPEDIA: GENEVA SHOW CANCELLED 2020 · DEPOSITS, PAYMENT SCHEDULE: NOT STATED

scenes.text: The Backfire report also mentions three more Czinger models, one of them lower-priced. No price, date or specification is given. If a cheaper model arrives, it would change the economics for the company, and arguably the value of the first eighty. That is speculation on our part, so we mark it as such, and we leave it there.
scenes.caption: BACKFIRE: 3 ADDITIONAL MODELS PLANNED, INCL. A LOWER-PRICED ONE · PRICE / DATE / SPECS: NOT STATED · EFFECT ON FIRST 80 CARS' VALUE = OUR SPECULATION

scenes.text: Numbers this large are hard to feel. Two reference points we have from earlier research on this channel: Kelley Blue Book put the average price of a new vehicle in the United States at fifty thousand eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six, and the Census Bureau put median household income for twenty twenty-four at eighty-three thousand seven hundred thirty dollars. Those are context, not claims about the Czinger.
scenes.caption: KELLEY BLUE BOOK (AUG 2026): AVERAGE NEW VEHICLE $50,089 · U.S. CENSUS BUREAU (2024): MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME $83,730 · CONTEXT ONLY; NOT SOURCES ABOUT THE CZINGER
scenes.chapter: Putting one point seven million in context

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, one point seven million dollars is about thirty-four average new vehicles. At two million, it is about forty. Against median household income, one point seven million is about twenty years of a typical household's pre-tax income, and the three hundred thousand dollar gap between the two reported prices alone is about three and a half years.
scenes.caption: 1,700,000 ÷ 50,089 = 33.9 · 2,000,000 ÷ 50,089 = 39.9 · 1,700,000 ÷ 83,730 = 20.3 YEARS · 300,000 ÷ 83,730 = 3.6 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC; INCOME PRE-TAX, MEDIAN)

scenes.text: That does not mean the price is unreasonable or reasonable. A hypercar is not priced against a daily driver. It is priced against other hypercars and against what a small group of buyers will pay. Our sources do not describe the buyers. They do not say who ordered the Czinger, how many were sold out, or whether there is a waiting list.
scenes.caption: BUYER PROFILE, ORDER BOOK, WAITING LIST: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · 'NOT PRICED AGAINST A DAILY DRIVER' = OUR READING

scenes.text: So the context scenes are perspective, not evidence of value. A price can look huge compared with income and still be modest compared with other hypercars, or the reverse. We prefer to give the arithmetic and leave the judgement to you, since no source in our set evaluates whether one point seven million dollars is fair for what the car does.
scenes.caption: NO SOURCE EVALUATES FAIRNESS OF THE PRICE · PERSPECTIVE ≠ VALUE JUDGEMENT

scenes.text: The sources name several cost drivers but give no figures. ASME lists laser-metal printing of the rear subframe, robotic assembly with laser-tracked positioning, in-house adhesives, a proprietary aluminium alloy for the gearbox case, and a computational optimizer. Wikipedia lists an in-house V8, an axial-flux motor and a lithium-titanate battery. Each of those has a cost, and none is given.
scenes.caption: ASME: LASER-METAL PRINTING, ROBOT CELL, IN-HOUSE ADHESIVES, PROPRIETARY ALUMINIUM ALLOY, TOPOLOGY OPTIMIZER · WIKIPEDIA: V8, AXIAL-FLUX MGU, LITHIUM-TITANATE BATTERY · COSTS: NOT STATED FOR ANY OF THEM
scenes.chapter: Where the money goes, according to the sources

scenes.text: Even the wheels are unusual. Wikipedia says the brake caliper and upright are one unit called the BrakeNode. If a normal car has a caliper bolted to a separate carrier, then replacing a damaged part might be simple. If the two are one printed piece, replacing one may mean replacing both. That is a reasonable question for an owner, but no source answers it.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: BRAKENODE = CALIPER + UPRIGHT IN ONE UNIT · REPLACEMENT COST / PROCEDURE: NOT STATED · QUESTION IS OUR OWN, NOT A SOURCE'S

scenes.text: Engineering effort is the largest cost the sources hint at. Facfox says Divergent was launched in twenty fourteen, and grew within three years into what it calls an over one hundred million dollar venture. ASME says Divergent has existed for eight to ten years with the mission of toolless manufacturing. Years of development sit behind every 21C, and the sources give no way to allocate them.
scenes.caption: FACFOX: DIVERGENT LAUNCHED 2014; 'OVER $100M VENTURE' WITHIN 3 YEARS · ASME (2025): 'EIGHT TO 10 YEARS' · ALLOCATION OF DEVELOPMENT COST PER CAR: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Part of that effort is shared. The ASME article says McLaren and Bugatti have begun working with Divergent on printed structural components. If other carmakers pay Divergent, the development cost is spread beyond the 21C. We do not know the terms of those deals, or how much revenue they bring. It is a reason the car's price may not reflect its full development cost.
scenes.caption: ASME (2025): McLAREN + BUGATTI 'HAVE BEGUN WORKING WITH DIVERGENT' ON PRINTED STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS · TERMS, REVENUE: NOT STATED · 'PRICE MAY NOT REFLECT FULL DEVELOPMENT COST' = OUR READING

scenes.text: Let us grade the figures. The one point seven million dollar price: one source, dated March twenty twenty-four, no price list. The two million figure: one source, dated twenty twenty, explicitly unconfirmed. The three to four thousand hours: one source, with no definition. The five hundred million raised: one source, from the founder, in twenty twenty-two.
scenes.caption: $1.7 M: ONE SOURCE (BACKFIRE, 2024) · $2 M: ONE SOURCE (GTPLANET, 2020, 'UNCONFIRMED') · 3,000–4,000 H: ONE SOURCE (BACKFIRE), UNDEFINED · ~$500 M: ONE SOURCE (CSQ, 2022, FOUNDER'S STATEMENT)
scenes.chapter: How confident are we in each number?

scenes.text: By contrast, the Senna's seven hundred fifty thousand pound price appears in Autocar, GoAuto and Wikipedia, so it is much better supported. The auction result of one point nine million pounds is on Wikipedia alone. So the Senna's price side has more confirmation than the Czinger's, which is itself a finding about how openly each company shares numbers.
scenes.caption: SENNA £750,000: AUTOCAR + GOAUTO + WIKIPEDIA · SENNA AUCTION £1,916,793: WIKIPEDIA ONLY · 'HOW OPENLY EACH COMPANY SHARES NUMBERS' = OUR READING FROM SOURCE COUNT

scenes.text: Where would we look for better numbers? A manufacturer's price list, a delivery receipt, a published auction result, an independent weighing, an insurance quote, a service invoice. None is in our set. If you own a 21C or know someone who does, those documents would answer more questions than any article we have read, and we would be glad to see them.
scenes.caption: DOCUMENTS THAT WOULD HELP (NOT IN OUR SOURCES): PRICE LIST · DELIVERY RECEIPT · AUCTION RESULT · INDEPENDENT WEIGHING · INSURANCE QUOTE · SERVICE INVOICE

scenes.text: A final note on tone. A video like this can sound like it is doubting the car. We are not. Lap times, printed parts and a funded company are real. Our job is to separate what the sources prove from what they merely repeat, so you can decide how much to trust a headline cost number when you see one in a comment section.
scenes.caption: METHOD NOTE · PROVEN: LAP TIMES (WIKIPEDIA), PRINTED PARTS (ASME), FUNDING STATEMENT (CSQ) · MERELY REPEATED: PRICE, HOURS, SPEED, WEIGHT

scenes.text: Now the cost nobody likes to discuss: running one. Our sources contain no insurance quote for the Czinger, no service price, no tyre price, no fuel consumption figure, and no reliability data. The same is true for the Senna. For two cars of this kind, the missing running cost is likely large, but we do not have a source for a number.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES (EITHER CAR): INSURANCE · SERVICE · TYRES · FUEL ECONOMY · RELIABILITY

scenes.text: One piece of design may bear on that. ASME says the BrakeNode combines the caliper and the knuckle into one structure, lowering part count and simplifying assembly. Fewer parts can mean fewer things to fail, but also a more expensive part to replace. The article gives no price or service guidance, so which way it cuts for an owner is unknown.
scenes.caption: ASME: BRAKENODE = CALIPER + KNUCKLE, 'LOWERS PART COUNT, SIMPLIFIES ASSEMBLY, IMPROVES RIGIDITY' · REPLACEMENT PRICE / SERVICE GUIDANCE: NOT STATED · OWNER IMPACT = OUR SPECULATION

scenes.text: The fuel is a different case. CSQ says the 21C is net-zero in emissions when run on carbon-recycled methanol. That is a fuel claim. The article does not say the car is sold with it, where to buy it, or what it costs. For an owner, the practical question is whether the car runs on ordinary fuel, and our sources do not say.
scenes.caption: CSQ (SEP 2022): 'NET-ZERO EMISSIONS WHEN RUN ON CARBON-RECYCLED METHANOL' · AVAILABILITY / COST OF THAT FUEL: NOT STATED · ORDINARY-FUEL OPERATION: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Some of what you pay for is performance, and that can be measured. Wikipedia lists a Laguna Seca lap of one minute twenty-two point three zero on the fifteenth of December twenty twenty-five. The Senna's time, per McLaren, was one twenty-seven sixty-two. By our arithmetic, the Czinger is five point three two seconds quicker, about six percent.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 21C 1:22.30 (15 DEC 2025) · McLAREN RELEASE VIA DUPONT REGISTRY: SENNA 1:27.62 · 87.62 − 82.30 = 5.32 S = 6.1% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CONDITIONS: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Whether that is worth a price difference is a personal call, and our sources do not let us compute it. We have different currencies, different years, a Senna price from list and a Czinger price from a news report. What we can say is that the faster car is also the more expensive one in nominal terms, and that the sources do not show a cheaper car matching it.
scenes.caption: £750,000 (2017 LIST) vs $1.7 M (2024 REPORT) — NOT DIRECTLY COMPARABLE · 'NOT SHOWN A CHEAPER CAR MATCHING IT' = ABSENCE IN OUR SOURCES, NOT PROOF

scenes.text: So what is the real cost of a three-D-printed hypercar? The visible part is one point seven million dollars, reported, with an earlier figure of two million. The hidden parts are three to four thousand labour hours per car, a company funded at close to half a billion dollars together with its sister firm, and years of waiting. The invisible part is running cost, and that is simply not documented.
scenes.caption: SUMMARY: PRICE $1.7 M (2024) / ~$2 M (2020) · 3,000–4,000 LABOR HOURS · ~$500 M RAISED (CZINGER + DIVERGENT) · DELIVERIES 3.6+ YEARS AFTER UNVEILING · RUNNING COSTS: NOT DOCUMENTED

scenes.text: We left out any claim that the printing makes the car cheaper to build, because no source gives a build cost. We left out any resale prediction, because the Czinger has no sourced resale results. And we left out price comparisons across currencies, because the sources give no rates. If you see a confident number for any of those, ask where it came from.
scenes.caption: LEFT OUT (NO SOURCE): BUILD COST · RESALE PREDICTION · CROSS-CURRENCY PRICE COMPARISON · ANY OF THESE WITHOUT A CITED SOURCE SHOULD BE TREATED AS A GUESS

scenes.text: That is the real cost of a three-D-printed hypercar, as far as the sources can take us. If you enjoyed this, subscribe to Pickup Reality and tell us which exotic car's cost you want checked next. Every source is in the description, along with the dates, so you can see which numbers are old. We will see you in the next one.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY · SOURCES + DATES IN THE DESCRIPTION
